html:
Andean states and chiefdoms is the map's label for the many local powers of the Andes between the fall of Wari and Tiwanaku around 1000 and the rise of the Inca. Archaeologists call these centuries the Late Intermediate Period.

With no empire over them, the highlands broke into many small chiefdoms and kingdoms. People lived in kin groups called ayllus, which held land together and shared work. They farmed potatoes, maize and quinoa on terraces and herded llamas and alpacas. They often built their towns on defended hilltops, which suggests frequent war.

Some grew strong:

  • Chimor, the coastal kingdom of the Chimú, with its capital at Chan Chan
  • the Aymara kingdoms around Lake Titicaca
  • the Chanka, rivals of the early Inca
  • the Chachapoya of the cloud forest, builders of Kuelap

One small kingdom around Cusco grew into the Inca Empire in the 1400s and absorbed nearly all the others.
